_comment: Millbrook town runtime config. Cells are the 65x65 town grid; an NPC cell is the character's FEET (bottom-centre), matching scripts/render_town_hero_proof.py and scripts/place_town_npcs.py. ids and dialogueKeys are FIXED by the frozen bundle -- quests turn in against them -- so they are not free to rename.

npcs.name: Sage
npcs.text: I have read these woods for forty years. The old paths still hold, if you know where to set your feet. Bring me what you find out there and I will tell you what it means.

npcs.name: Healer
npcs.text: Sit down and let me look at you. I can heal your wounds, and there is no charge for anyone who walked in through that gate.

npcs.name: Miller
npcs.text: That wheel has turned every day since my father's time. Grain from the fields, flour for the whole valley. Mind the bridge planks, they are wet through.

npcs.name: Herbalist
npcs.text: Everything worth picking grows along the stream bank. Stay on this side of it, though. What grows past the water belongs to the woods.

npcs.name: Shopkeeper
npcs.text: Take a look at my wares, traveller.

exit.note: Exit lands on the overworld, and the AUTHORITY is public/act1-world-map.js's LANDMARKS entry for this town -- `EXITS[mapId] = L.exit`, the open cell beside its door. NOT src/data/maps.ts. maps.ts's connection (100,321) is legacy: the Act 1 override REWRITES it at runtime, but only inside scene.checkTransition, which is the SHIPPED town's edge-exit path. A hi-fi town never goes through it -- adapter.js's act1-town-exit handler assigns scene.heroTileX/heroTileY = data.toX/toY directly -- so for these towns the value here is used RAW and must already be the landmark exit. || IN-TOWN HALF RE-MEASURED 2026-08-24 AGAINST THE PAINTING. Owner, on build 57: "the in-town exit does not match what we see on screen." He was right, and it was the same defect in all three towns: `cell` sat 2.5-3.5 cells BEYOND the drawn gate, out on the open trail, so the player walked visibly out of the village and kept going before the screen changed. Millbrook's fence line measures at cell y=56 by timber_mask (12.6 / 21.5 / 10.6 % of rows 55/56/57 against under 1% either side); greenhollow's at y=55.5; Port Sapphire has no gate and its mouth is where the trail leaves the frame at y=0. The old cells -- 60.5, 59.0 and 3.0 -- predate the current paintings. || `cell` is now the GATE AS PAINTED and `startCell` is 3.5 cells INSIDE it. That combination is what makes town.html's arming work without a code change: it arms once the player is more than 2.5 cells clear, so a 3.5-cell spawn is armed on arrival but outside the dy<1.0 / dx<1.6 fire box, and the exit then fires exactly when she steps into the gate. The previous arrangement solved the same arming problem the other way round -- exit outside, spawn on the gate -- which is what put the trigger out in the grass. || The OVERWORLD half (toX/toY) is unchanged and still gated by scripts/check_town_transitions.py. || MOVED TO THE MAP EDGE 2026-08-29. OWNER on build 62: "the exit of the town is set at a weird place too. i want the exit to be set to the edge of the town map (all towns)." This REVERSES the in-town half of the 2026-08-24 change above, which put `cell` on the gate as painted; the owner has now seen both and picked the edge, so the edge is the decision. Every town is 65 cells square, so the edge cell centre is 64.5 on a south mouth and 0.5 on a north one, and the whole trail from the gate to the frame is walkable -- verified against the walkable authority by BFS from startCell, which reaches cy 64.38 (greenhollow), 64.31 (millbrook) and 0.50 (portSapphire). `startCell` is UNCHANGED and stays at the gate: arming only needs the spawn to be more than 2.5 cells clear of the exit, which a 11.5-12.5 cell gap satisfies far more comfortably than the old 3.5, and moving the arrival cell to the edge would drop the player a dozen cells outside her own town on every re-entry. The fire box (dy < 1.0, dx < 1.6) was checked reachable at each new exit before this was written. The OVERWORLD half (toX/toY) is untouched and still gated by scripts/check_town_transitions.py. || MOVED BACK TO THE TOWN'S MOUTH 2026-08-29, and the TEST CHANGED WITH IT. OWNER on build 63: "the player needs to exit the town the moment they touch the edge of the town. currently they need to walk off of the map to exit it." The map-edge exit of build 63 was literally what he asked for the day before and still wrong to play, because the 65-cell canvas is bigger than the painted town: greenhollow's village stops at the fence around y 56 and the remaining eight cells are an empty grass apron. `cell` is now the MOUTH -- the first row where the reachable ground narrows to the single trail, measured by BFS from startCell: greenhollow y 57.0 (x 30.31-34.06), millbrook y 59.0 (x 29.31-33.88), Port Sapphire y 4.0 (x 31.44-33.75). town.html no longer uses a symmetric box around this point; it fires when the player CROSSES the line, which is what makes 'the moment they touch it' true and what stops the old box firing a cell early on the way out -- the defect behind the build-62 complaint. The OVERWORLD half (toX/toY) is untouched and still gated by scripts/check_town_transitions.py.

_dialogueNote: name/text are English FALLBACK strings in the voice of the shipped Port Sapphire entries, so the town is playable standalone. The runtime also posts act1-town-interact to the parent so the bundle's real localised dialogue system can take over once the adapter hands off. ids and dialogueKeys match the frozen bundle: sage is a quest turn-in.
_layoutNote: REPLACED 2026-08-22. These cells no longer come from design/act1-towns/millbrook/spec.json: scripts/town_layout.py wrote that file for the plan-primed layout the owner scrapped, and the village was repainted afterwards, so its snapping described geometry the art no longer has -- savePoint sat on a cottage roof. Towns are ART-FIRST: the painting is authored, scripts/derive_town_walkable.py derives collision from the finished plate, and scripts/place_town_actors.py places the actors against THAT, eroding by actorFootRadius so the body fits rather than the point and flood-filling from startCell so nothing sits in a courtyard the player cannot enter. Re-run that script rather than hand-editing; it verifies as well as writes, and it reported every actor here standable and reachable.
_foregroundNote: Millbrook has no foreground layer, and `foreground` is optional in town.html -- the key is omitted rather than pointed at a file that does not exist.
_serviceNote: shopCounter stands on the lane in front of the market stall's produce counter, and shopId matches the inventory src/data/shops.ts already defines. savePoint MOVED 2026-08-22: [37,41] was valid against the scrapped plan-primed collision and lands on the brown cottage's ROOF in the painted village; it is now the paving just south of the well, which is where the save point reads.
_shopkeeperNote: MOVED OUT IN FRONT 2026-08-24. Owner, on build 58: "the shop keeper is placed on top of the shop so lets put him in front of the shop." He was standing INSIDE the stall, three to four cells above shopCounter and level with the hanging produce, which from a top-down camera reads as standing ON the stall rather than behind its counter -- the 2026-08-22 note below asked for him to be findable in his shop and this was the wrong way to give him that. He now stands on the lane beside the counter, on ground the player walks on, so he is a person in front of a shop. || `fixed` is DROPPED with him: it existed only because the inside of a stall is deliberately not walkable and snapping him would have thrown him out onto the lane -- which is now where he is meant to be. scripts/place_town_actors.py places and validates him like every other NPC, including the talk-band check. || Tapping him still opens the shipped ShopScene rather than a dialogue box, so the town never forks the inventory or the prices, and shopCounter remains the service spot in front of the stall. || PREVIOUS NOTE: Owner 2026-08-22: "i cannot find the shopkeeper and the shopkeeper needs to be in a shop." He stands INSIDE the market stall, behind the counter, which is why he carries `fixed: true` -- scripts/place_town_actors.py snaps actors onto walkable ground and the inside of a stall is deliberately not walkable, so snapping him would put him out on the lane. town.html routes a tap on him to the shop the same way it routes the healer to the heal flow, so the shipped ShopScene stays the single implementation. shopCounter remains the spot in FRONT of the stall where the player stands.
_startNote: MOVED 2026-08-24 from [32.5, 57.0] to [32.5, 53.0]: 3.5 cells inside the painted gate, which is what arms the exit on arrival without firing it. See exit.note.
